reviewReasons.requirements: The spec and diff cover all seven ACs, but the spec says PUT while the API uses PATCH, and it doesn't pin down the 30 February case or the date's wire format.
reviewReasons.scope: The change stays on the feature; the hand-written JSON parsing, which loosens validation of title and done, and the plan and spec files are side effects of the chosen design.
reviewReasons.tests: Store, API and prerendered page tests cover most behaviour, but there is no test for an impossible date such as 30 February or a non-string dueDate, and the live filter toggle is untested. No existing tests were weakened.
reviewReasons.conventions: It uses ValidationException for 400s, data-testid on the new elements, and xUnit tests in the existing style; the manual JsonElement parsing departs from the repo's typed-binding idiom.
reviewReasons.architecture: The overdue logic is shared in TodoStore.IsOverdue, but hand-parsing request bodies in Program.cs and the tri-state TodoPatch with a secondary constructor are heavier than needed. An anonymous-object ToDto helper also sits in Program.cs.
reviewReasons.codeQuality: The `when` guards silently ignore a dueDate of the wrong type, such as a number, instead of returning 400, which breaks AC3. A non-object body would likely cause a 500, and the response serializes dueDate as a full UTC timestamp rather than a plain date.

reviewReasons.requirements: All seven acceptance criteria are covered in the spec and the diff, but the spec says nothing about the 400 body shape for POST, where `DateOnly?` binding errors don't go through the `ValidationException` path.
reviewReasons.scope: The change stays on the feature; the only extras are the plan and spec docs under docs/, which are low-risk.
reviewReasons.tests: The store, API and page tests are good and no existing test was weakened. The 'nur überfällige' toggle behaviour has no test, the POST 400 tests check only the status code, and the PATCH tests never cover a non-object body.
reviewReasons.conventions: AGENTS.md says `TodoStore` throws `ValidationException`, but the date validation lives in `Program.cs`'s `ParsePatch`. POST relies on JSON binding errors instead, so its 400 body may not be the `{"error": ...}` shape.
reviewReasons.architecture: The hand-rolled `JsonElement` parser in `Program.cs`, plus a `DueDateSet` flag on `TodoPatch`, puts parsing and validation in the wrong layer. The two input paths also validate differently: POST uses framework binding, PATCH uses `TryParseExact`.
reviewReasons.codeQuality: `ParsePatch` throws `InvalidOperationException`, giving a 500, when the body isn't a JSON object, because `TryGetProperty` is called on a non-object. It also silently ignores wrongly typed `title` and `done` values, and POST and PATCH accept different date formats.

reviewReasons.requirements: The spec and diff cover AC1–AC7 (optional date, set/change/remove, 400 on invalid dates, overdue filter, display, marker, toggle); the spec's PATCH section is somewhat muddled, but the behaviour is clear.
reviewReasons.scope: The changes stay on the feature; the only extras are the spec and plan markdown files and the extra public factory overloads and test helpers.
reviewReasons.tests: Store and API tests cover the date logic, validation and the overdue filter well, but the page test only checks that the testids and the word appear and never that non-overdue todos lack the marker. The toggle's filtering behaviour is not tested. Existing tests were adapted to the new signatures, not weakened.
reviewReasons.conventions: The code reuses ValidationException and the existing 400 middleware and uses German UI text and testids as the spec asks, but the `NewTodo.Of` factory workaround and the `default` JsonElement arguments in tests depart from the plain record style used before.
reviewReasons.architecture: The clock and the overdue predicate sit in TodoStore and the page reads the store directly, which fits. Using raw JsonElement in the public DTO records, with TodoJson and ToElement helpers living in production code mainly to serve tests, is a leaky and awkward design.
reviewReasons.codeQuality: The behaviour is correct at the edges (strict format, UTC today, null versus missing), but the JsonElement-based records with overloaded Of factories are needlessly complex, and the JsonException catch could mask unrelated errors.
